assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based account of technology and the empirical trade-shock literature changed how economists and policymakers understand wage inequality, labour-market adjustment and the political consequences of economic change. The identification strategies are credible and the questions are of first-order importance.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the central figure for the task framework and the empirical polarisation evidence. Autor and Hanson are the core of the China-shock work. Dorn and Katz are important co-authors but more junior or more tied to other bodies of work. Task-model theory also owes much to others outside the credited set (for example Acemoglu), so the credit is somewhat diffuse.
assessment.maturity: The work spans roughly 2003 to 2016 and has been replicated, extended and contested for years. It has had time to be tested, including critiques of the shock design and of long-run effects.
uncertainties: Committee judgment on whether a two-person prize is cleanly separable from the task literature's other contributors.
Ongoing debate over the long-run size of trade-shock effects and over how general the findings are.
Overlap with recent recognition of work on technology and institutions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their political-economy models of trade protection and, more broadly, their endogenous-growth and trade framework are foundational and shaped decades of trade theory and policy analysis. The conceptual contribution is deep and clearly their own.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is unusually clean, with a long-standing and well-defined two-person partnership. Helpman also appears in the firm-heterogeneity candidate, which suggests the credit for his broader body of work is large.
assessment.maturity: The central results date from the 1990s and have been tested, extended and widely taught. There are no timing concerns, though age and the passage of time are a consideration.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to reward the political-economy-of-protection strand or the broader trade and growth strand, which affects how the citation is framed.
Direct empirical validation of the lobbying model is mixed.
Potential overlap with the Melitz-related firm-heterogeneity work in trade.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work built modern political economics: how electoral rules, constitutions and state capacity shape fiscal policy and development. It has produced large theoretical and empirical literatures and links economics to the study of institutions.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the clear anchors through their joint programme on constitutions and policy outcomes. Besley's work on state capacity and accountability is separate but closely related. Others in the field, such as Acemoglu, Alesina and Dixit, have contributed or have been recognised, so the boundaries of the prize need care.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the 1990s through the 2010s and is mature, though the causal evidence on constitutional effects remains debated. The 2024 prize on institutions may narrow the room for further recognition in this area.
uncertainties: Disclosed conflict: I have co-authored with Persson, and my field overlaps heavily with this candidate. I weigh that against the merits but have not adjudicated it.
Causal identification of constitutional effects is contested.
Whether the committee sees this as too close to the 2024 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and the financial accelerator offered a formal account of how credit frictions amplify and propagate shocks. The 2008 crisis made this framework central to macroeconomics and policy.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore's credit-cycles model and the Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist financial accelerator are the two pillars. Bernanke's absence from the credited list, along with his earlier prize, complicates a clean three-person attribution. Gertler also appears in the New Keynesian candidate.
assessment.maturity: The foundational papers date from 1989 to 1999, and the framework has been heavily used and extended, particularly after 2008. The timing is mature.
uncertainties: Awkward credit split between the Kiyotaki-Moore and Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist strands.
Overlap with the New Keynesian and macro-finance candidates.
Empirical performance of the models in quantitative settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities underpins how central banks think about monetary policy, covering policy rules, inflation targeting and the transmission mechanism. Its practical and intellectual impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the main difficulty. Eight names are credited, spanning price-setting (Calvo), policy rules (Taylor), the canonical framework (Woodford, Gali, Gertler) and medium-scale DSGE estimation (Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets). Any three-person selection leaves out major contributors such as Clarida.
assessment.maturity: The work from the 1980s to the early 2000s is very mature, and the framework has been tested through multiple episodes. It is now being revised through heterogeneous-agent extensions.
uncertainties: Large attribution problem, and the chosen trio is one of several defensible alternatives.
The framework's performance in the post-pandemic inflation episode is debated.
Overlap with the financial-accelerator and HANK candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The top-income series built from tax records transformed the empirical study of inequality and reshaped public debate and the research agenda. The data contribution is substantial and has become an international standard.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the pioneers of the long-run top-income series. Zucman's offshore-wealth work is more recent and more contested. Saez also appears in the optimal-tax candidate, which suggests broader credit for him.
assessment.maturity: The foundational top-incomes work dates from around 2001 to 2003 and is mature. The wealth-tax, capital-in-the-twenty-first-century and offshore estimates are still being contested.
uncertainties: Methodological critiques of some wealth and distributional estimates.
Whether the committee treats this mainly as a data contribution or as a theoretical one.
Policy prominence may colour how the contribution is perceived.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data opened large-scale, credible measurement of intergenerational mobility and of neighbourhood effects. This has changed empirical work in public and labour economics and influenced policy design.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear leader and Hendren is the main co-author on the neighbourhood-effects results. Friedman and Katz are significant collaborators, and Chetty also appears in the optimal-tax candidate. A narrow prize would leave out many co-authors.
assessment.maturity: The key papers date from 2014 to 2022, which makes this relatively recent. Replication and longer-run follow-up of the neighbourhood effects are still developing.
uncertainties: The maturity of recent work and whether the causal neighbourhood estimates will hold up over time.
The extent to which the contribution is data and measurement versus conceptual.
Large team-based credit makes a short laureate list difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework showed how distortions in resource allocation across firms can account for large cross-country income differences. It supplies a tractable bridge between micro data and aggregate productivity and has become standard in development and growth.
assessment.attribution: The 2009 Hsieh-Klenow paper is the core, with Restuccia and Rogerson's related work as an important parallel. Restuccia is credited here, but a two-person selection reflects the Hsieh-Klenow paper's centrality.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from 2008 to 2009 and has been extended for over fifteen years, including in applications to specific economies. Some measurement concerns have emerged.
uncertainties: Debate over whether measured dispersion in marginal products reflects true distortions or measurement error.
Proximity to the parallel Restuccia-Rogerson contribution.
Relative standing versus other growth and development candidates.
